title: How to build a pyramid structure
coreMove: Build the hierarchy from raw material upward, letting classification and order create the top sentence instead of forcing a headline early.
sourcePressure: Chapter 3 is construction discipline: bottom-up approach, caveats for beginners, grouping raw material, ordering it, and letting the higher-order idea emerge before top-down delivery.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Starting with a confident top line and hunting for support afterward.

sourceAnchors.name: bottom-up approach
sourceAnchors.detail: the authorized heading map for Chapter 3 includes The bottom-up approach and Caveats for beginners
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The beginner caveat is simple: an early headline is often a guess wearing a suit.

hook: A polished heading pretends the structure underneath is solved

counterintuition: Most people think formatting solves clarity; actually thinking solves clarity

structure sounds rigid but actually creates freedom

ask yourself what the point is

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective recognition, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm through a direct second-person passage, a short research/source aside, a reader question, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: a pharmaceutical trial coordinator building a site-readiness update
exampleSpecs.audience: clinical operations staff with scattered site data
exampleSpecs.stakes: trial launch dates depend on whether readiness problems are regulatory, staffing, or supply related
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Claire dumps all site notes into one sheet, color-codes them by function, and waits to write the readiness answer until the clusters settle.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Cold fluorescent light reflects off a binder of site-initiation notes.

exampleSpecs.domain: a documentary producer structuring interview footage for a funding cut
exampleSpecs.audience: creative leads who need argument before edit
exampleSpecs.stakes: a grant renewal reel will fail if it follows shoot chronology instead of the point the footage proves
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "The first interview is not the first point," Mathieu says, then groups clips by claim before naming the reel's opening argument.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "The first interview is not the first point," Mathieu says under the edit-suite hum.

exampleSpecs.domain: a food-bank analyst converting donation logs into a capacity request
exampleSpecs.stakes: warehouse staffing may be rejected if volume, spoilage, and route constraints stay mixed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Rachel keeps the old headline visible, groups the logs into volume, spoilage, and route constraints, then replaces the headline with the narrower answer the groups can bear.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Rachel four donation logs to stop defending the first headline.

exampleSpecs.domain: a marine insurer assessing storm-damage claims
exampleSpecs.stakes: premiums will be mispriced if vessel age, mooring quality, and storm exposure are forced into one story
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Henrik predicts vessel age will govern the answer, then lets the grouped evidence reveal that mooring quality is the stronger parent line.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What if the oldest boats were not the risky ones?

exampleSpecs.domain: a telecom service designer building a customer-complaint hierarchy
exampleSpecs.audience: service teams converting call logs into product priorities
exampleSpecs.stakes: the wrong top line could fund app changes while billing confusion causes most calls
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Aanya refuse the product team's preferred headline, group calls by failure type, and let billing confusion rise to the parent claim.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You are looking at 240 call tags blinking in a service dashboard.
mustAvoid: support ticket bug-priority scene from ch1

exampleSpecs.domain: a theater production manager preparing a rehearsal-risk note
exampleSpecs.audience: arts administrators coordinating sets, cast, and permits
exampleSpecs.stakes: opening night slips if the risk memo follows anecdotes instead of grouped constraints
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 6:45 p.m., Jack pulls notes off the rehearsal-room door, separates permit risks from set risks, and writes the governing warning only after the split.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 6:45 p.m., Jack peels curling notes from a black rehearsal-room door.

skillTargets: choose bottom-up construction when the answer is not earned
classify raw material by logical function
revise the top line after grouping changes

tryThisNowSpec: Dump ten facts from a live draft into a blank note. Group them by logical job, order each group, then write the parent sentence last.
